source of assertPlainObject()/assertDigest() exact-schema guards reused by reconcile.mjs.

purpose: This unit is the Phase-1 (manual, single-cycle, requirementsRevision=56) 'holder distribution' pipeline: given a closed cycle's proceeds and an off-chain HKMN holder snapshot, it (1) validates/binds a candidate distribution of the returned USDG pro rata to holders (reconcile.mjs), (2) builds a canonical, Solidity-parity Merkle-sum tree of up to 1024 payout leaves and verifies an owner Ed25519 signature over it (manifest.mjs), (3) re-derives the tree from three independent byte-identical 'copies' (primary/mirror/archive) and produces a second, independently-signed verification receipt (manifest.mjs), and (4) exposes a pure keccak256/tagged-hash implementation (merkle-sum.mjs / canonical-merkle-sum.mjs) whose output is fed via Foundry FFI into a Solidity payout-verifier so the JS tree and the on-chain tree are proven byte-for-byte identical for one recipient. Everything here is explicitly scoped 'LOCAL' / 'FIXTURE' / 'NOT_LIVE_FUNDING_AUTHORITY' -- it prepares a signed authorization object; it does not itself move funds, call an RPC, or read a live snapshot.

reconcile.mjs: deriveClosedProceedsBasis(handoffValue) -> basis object with basisDigest; pure, re-derives all digests from the handoff and throws if anything (ledger digest, proceeds key, custody separation, USDG-only, activity-isolated pre/post balance delta) fails to match. No I/O.

deriveHolderDistributionCandidate({closedProceedsBasis, snapshot, entries}) -> candidate object (status 'PENDING_OWNER_APPROVAL_AND_PROOF_DOMAIN') with candidateDigest/snapshotDigest/entriesDigest. Validates 1..1024 dense entries, strictly increasing indices 0..1023, unique nonzero recipients, each entry's directHkmnBalance equal to the matching snapshot balance, and sum(amountAtomicUSDG) === closedProceedsBasis.finalCredit.amount exactly.
merkle-sum.mjs / canonical-merkle-sum.mj: DEPTH=10, WIDTH=1024, TAGS (domain-separation tags), buildDistribution({domain, snapshotNumber, snapshotHash, entries}) -> {manifestBytes, manifestDigest, leaves, root, proofs} building all 1024 leaves (nonemptyLeaf/emptyLeaf) and a fixed-depth-10 sum-Merkle tree.
manifestBytes(...) -> canonical ABI-style hex encoding (head + entry count + entries); decodeCanonicalManifest(hex) round-trips and re-checks manifestBytes(decoded) === input for canonicality.

verifyProof(leaf, index, proof, expectedRoot), orderedProofsDigest(proofs) (keccak fold over all 1024 proofs, requires exactly WIDTH proofs), keccak256() (from-scratch Keccak-f[1600] in BigInt, no library).
manifest.mjs: distributionApprovalDigest(payload), distributionVerificationDigest(value) -- domain-tagged sha256 digests (via journal.digest), not the on-chain keccak.

verifyDistributionVerificationReceipt(value) -- checks exact schema, authority strings, digest/bytes32 field shapes, non-zero bytes32s, exactly 3 unique non-empty sourceIds with copyCount===3, receipt self-digest, and an Ed25519 signature from a hardcoded DISTRIBUTION_VERIFIER_PUBLIC_KEY.

compileApprovedDistribution({closedProceedsBasis, snapshot, entries, approval}) -> the 'canonical-holder-distribution.v1' artifact (schema 'LOCAL_FIXTURE_VERIFIED_NOT_PUBLISHED'): re-derives the candidate, verifies the owner-signed approval binds to it (chainId/hook/cycleId/payoutId/snapshotNumber/snapshotHash), builds the Merkle-sum tree, and asserts built.root.sum === candidate.totalAmountAtomicUSDG.

verifyDistributionCopies(artifact, copiesValue, contextValue) -> rebuilds the tree from the artifact's own entries, checks it against the stored manifest/root/proofsDigest/leaves, requires exactly 3 copies with distinct sourceIds whose manifestBytes are byte-identical to the artifact AND independently rebuild to the same manifestDigest/root/proofsDigest, binds a runner context (runnerCycleId/proceedsKey/closedLedgerDigest/closedProceedsBasisDigest/verificationJournalHead), and returns an unsigned verification-receipt payload (authority 'HOOKEMON_FIXTURE_DISTRIBUTION_VERIFIER', scope 'LOCAL_BYTES_ONLY_NOT_PUBLICATION_OR_LIVE_FUNDING_AUTHORITY').
cycle-runner.mjs (downstream, not in thi: runner.preparePayoutFunding({proceedsKey, verificationReceiptDigest, expiresAt, nonce}) -- requires a matching recorded receipt, builds a vaultPayoutAuthorization (authority 'LOCAL_PREPARATION_ONLY_NOT_LIVE_FUNDING_AUTHORITY'), and is nonce-replay-protected.

Explicitly absent: runner.compileAndPublishDistribution and runner.verifyIndependentDistribution do not exist (asserted `typeof ... === 'undefined'` in reconcile.test.mjs) -- there is no runner method that itself calls compileApprovedDistribution/verifyDistributionCopies; a human/operator script must do that off to the side and hand the runner only the final signed receipt.
integration adapter (script, not a test): phase-one-local-loop-adapter.mjs (argv: hookAddress, chainId) -- runs one full fixture cycle end-to-end in-process (open->...->return->closed->candidate->approval->artifact->3 copies->verification->preparePayoutFunding) and writes raw ABI-encoded bytes (LocalPayout struct: cycleId, payoutId, manifestDigest, rootHash, rootSum, recipient, amount, 10 sibling hashes, 10 sibling sums) to stdout. Invoked only via Foundry's vm.ffi from packages/contracts/test/integration/PhaseOneLocalLoop.t.sol; verified runnable standalone with `node test/integration/phase-one-local-loop-adapter.mjs <hook> <chainId>` (confirmed working during this review).

invariants: Every schema object in this unit is closed under exactObject/assertExactPlainObjectShape/assertPlainObject: no extra keys, no accessors/getters (own data properties only), no symbols, prototype must be plain Object.prototype -- this specifically defeats getter-based side-channel/tamper tricks (see holder-candidate.test.mjs 'dense and unadorned' / 'candidate accessor executed' test).

Holder candidate entries: 1..1024 entries, strictly increasing unique index in [0,1023], recipient must be a unique nonzero lowercase-hex EVM address, directHkmnBalance must be a positive decimal string EQUAL to the value at that recipient in the snapshot's directBalances, amountAtomicUSDG positive decimal, and SUM of all entries' amountAtomicUSDG must equal closedProceedsBasis.finalCredit.amount exactly (no more, no less) -- reconcile.mjs:329-333.

The module does NOT compute the pro-rata split itself. It only verifies that externally supplied per-entry amounts (a) individually match the snapshot balances and (b) sum exactly to the final USDG credit. No file in packages/runner computes amount = balance * proceeds / totalSupply anywhere (grep across src/ and test/ found nothing) -- rounding/remainder allocation is entirely the responsibility of a caller not present in this unit.

closedProceedsBasis custody separation: returnAccount === cycleVaultAccount, and operationsTrigger, cycleVaultAccount, policyAccount must be pairwise distinct (reconcile.mjs:219-224, re-checked at validateClosedProceedsBasis:257). finalCredit.asset must be exactly 'USDG', and postBalance-preBalance must equal amount exactly ('activity-isolated').

requirementsRevision is hardcoded to 56 (reconcile.mjs:201) -- this pins the module to the Phase-1/pre-Phase-2 policy revision; the deferred Phase-2 line uses revision 57 per the task's repository facts, so this unit will reject any Phase-2-shaped closed ledger.

Merkle-sum tree: fixed WIDTH=1024 (DEPTH=10) regardless of holder count; missing slots get a domain-tagged emptyLeaf(sum=0); parentNode enforces uint256 sum non-overflow; root.sum after a full build must equal candidate.totalAmountAtomicUSDG (manifest.mjs:245-247) -- i.e. the artifact-level check that the visible USDG total equals the tree's total, closing the loop between reconcile.mjs's sum check and the tree.

Three-copy quorum: verifyDistributionCopies requires exactly 3 entries in copiesValue, with 3 distinct non-empty sourceId strings, each copy's manifestBytes byte-identical to the artifact's, and each copy independently re-derived (via decodeCanonicalManifest + buildDistribution) to the same manifestDigest/root/proofsDigest. A single changed byte in any one copy is rejected (proven in manifest.test.mjs).

Owner approval binds ALL of: candidateDigest, closedProceedsBasisDigest, entriesDigest, chainId, cycleId, snapshotNumber, snapshotHash to the actual candidate/basis being compiled -- any mismatch throws 'distribution approval candidate binding is invalid' before the Ed25519 signature is even checked.

Every digest in this unit is a domain-tagged sha256 over canonicalJson() (see cycle/journal.mjs), which is a distinct hashing scheme from the on-chain/Solidity-parity keccak256 tagged hashes used inside the Merkle-sum tree itself (manifest/candidate/approval/receipt digests are off-chain bookkeeping hashes; leaf/node/manifest-tag hashes are the ones that must match Solidity).

decodeCanonicalManifest re-derives manifestBytes(decoded) and requires byte-equality with its input, rejecting any non-canonical (e.g. padded, reordered, or loosely-encoded) manifest -- this is what lets verifyDistributionCopies trust a copy's manifestBytes without re-trusting the sender.

Signing/verification uses two DISTINCT Ed25519 keypairs hardcoded in manifest.mjs: OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY (approves the candidate) and DISTRIBUTION_VERIFIER_PUBLIC_KEY (attests the 3-copy reconstruction). Both are literal DER hex constants in the source file, not loaded from config/env -- see keyFacts.
stateTransitions: Upstream (cycle-runner, out of unit): open -> ... -> return-finalized -> deriveClosedCycle() -> 'closed' -> consumeReturnedProceedsOnce(receiptDigest) [journals 'proceeds-consumed', mints a one-time proceedsKey] -> readClosedProceedsBasisHandoff(proceedsKey) [read-only, throws 'authenticated closed-cycle proceeds' if the key was never consumed via the store].

reconcile.deriveClosedProceedsBasis(handoff) -- pure/no side effects; can be called repeatedly and must be idempotent (reconcile.test.mjs asserts deepEqual across repeated calls and that cycleStore.snapshot is unchanged before/after).

reconcile.deriveHolderDistributionCandidate(...) -- pure; produces a candidate 'PENDING_OWNER_APPROVAL_AND_PROOF_DOMAIN'. No runner method exists to persist this candidate; it lives only in the caller's memory/output until an approval is produced externally.

manifest.compileApprovedDistribution(...) -- pure; requires an externally-produced, Ed25519-signed 'approval' object (schema hookemon.fixture-distribution-approval.v1, authority FIXTURE_OWNER_SIGNATURE) that itself must have been built and signed by code NOT in this unit (tests build+sign it inline with a raw private key). Produces the canonical artifact ('LOCAL_FIXTURE_VERIFIED_NOT_PUBLISHED').

manifest.verifyDistributionCopies(artifact, copies, context) -- pure; produces an UNSIGNED verification-receipt payload. Something outside this unit must sign it with the verifier's private key (again, only demonstrated inline in tests/the adapter script) before it is usable.

runner.recordDistributionVerification(signedReceipt) [in cycle-runner.mjs, downstream] -- calls manifest.verifyDistributionVerificationReceipt, journals 'distribution-verification-recorded'; idempotency/replay: calling twice on a reopened/recovered runner throws 'already recorded'.

runner.preparePayoutFunding({proceedsKey, verificationReceiptDigest, expiresAt, nonce}) [downstream] -- requires the exact recorded receipt to match both proceedsKey and receiptDigest; builds vaultPayoutAuthorization with authority 'LOCAL_PREPARATION_ONLY_NOT_LIVE_FUNDING_AUTHORITY'; nonce is replay-protected via a digest keyed store lookup (authorizationKeyForNonce); this is the terminal state this unit's data reaches inside the JS runner -- nothing after this point (actual on-chain submission) exists in packages/runner.

Tamper/recovery guarantees demonstrated in manifest.test.mjs: mutating a journaled vaultPayoutAuthorization's rootSum after the fact and replaying the journal through CycleRunner.recover throws 'vault authorization binding mismatch'; reopening a store and replaying the same journal produces byte-identical results and correctly rejects a second recordDistributionVerification/preparePayoutFunding call.
externalDependencies: packages/contracts/tooling/payout/canonical-merkle-sum.mjs -- the actual Merkle-sum/keccak implementation; merkle-sum.mjs is a thin re-export wrapper plus decodeCanonicalManifest. This crosses the runner/contracts package boundary via a relative '../../../contracts/tooling/payout/canonical-merkle-sum.mjs' import (no package dependency declared, just a path reach-through).
packages/runner/src/cycle/journal.mjs -- canonicalJson()/digest() (sha256-based, bounded-size canonicalization with recursion/size limits) used for every non-Merkle digest in this unit.
packages/runner/src/cycle/schemas.mjs -- assertPlainObject()/assertDigest() exact-shape validators reused by reconcile.mjs.

node:crypto -- createPublicKey/verify (Ed25519, 'sign(null, ...)' i.e. Ed25519ph-less pure Ed25519) for both owner-approval and copy-verification signatures; node:crypto sign() used only in tests/adapter, not in the reviewed src files.

Foundry/forge (external, not run by this review per instructions) -- packages/contracts/test/integration/PhaseOneLocalLoop.t.sol shells out via vm.ffi to the Node adapter and decodes its stdout as an ABI-encoded LocalPayout struct, then calls payEntitlement(...) on a Solidity contract with the same siblingHashes/siblingSums this unit produced -- this is the only place JS/Solidity Merkle-sum parity is actually cross-checked, and it is exercised for exactly one recipient (index 0) per run.

No network, RPC, chain client, price feed, or wallet library is imported anywhere in the 3 core files or the tests -- everything is deterministic, in-memory, and keyed off caller-supplied fixture objects.
testStatus: All 15 node:test cases in packages/runner/test/distribution/{holder-candidate,manifest,reconcile}.test.mjs pass under Node 24 (`node --test test/distribution/*.test.mjs`): 15 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, ~17.8s total (verified live during this review). No test in this set is marked .skip/.todo or is compile-only. packages/runner/test/integration/phase-one-local-loop-adapter.mjs is not a node:test file at all -- it is a plain script with no assertions of its own; its only checks are two inline `throw new Error(...)` guards (fixture return amount changed; local funding preparation differs from the canonical artifact) and it exits 0/prints hex on success. It was verified during this review to run standalone (`node test/integration/phase-one-local-loop-adapter.mjs <hook> <chainId>`) and to produce well-formed ABI-encoded output; its real 'test' role is only meaningful when invoked via Foundry's vm.ffi from PhaseOneLocalLoop.t.sol, which this review did NOT run (forge build/test explicitly forbidden by task instructions due to a concurrent baseline run). Coverage gaps: no test drives >2 real recipients through compileApprovedDistribution (boundary test at 1024 entries stops at candidate derivation and explicitly asserts no root/proof is created there); no test exercises verifyDistributionVerificationReceipt's or compileApprovedDistribution's behavior under a wrong-key signature (only truncated/sliced signatures are tested, e.g. manifest.test.mjs:257); no test constructs directBalances/entries with realistic (non-tiny) 1024-holder data to check performance of the O(1024) keccak-based tree build under load (each run of buildDistribution does 1024 leaf hashes + 1023 node hashes with a from-scratch BigInt Keccak-f, and one full test run of the 3-copy test alone took ~9.85s locally, suggesting non-trivial CPU cost if this were run every 20-minute cycle in production).
autonomyGaps: No pro-rata computation exists anywhere in this unit (or, per repo-wide grep, anywhere in packages/runner). For the owner's 'every N minutes, automatically distribute proceeds pro rata to holders' target, something must (a) take a live total-USDG-to-distribute + a live holder snapshot + total supply and compute each holder's amountAtomicUSDG with a defined rounding/remainder rule, before this unit's validation even starts. That computation is completely unimplemented and unspecified here (no remainder-handling code, no rounding-direction constant, nothing).

Every authority/scope string in this unit explicitly disclaims live use: 'LOCAL_FIXTURE_VERIFIED_NOT_PUBLISHED' (compileApprovedDistribution), 'LOCAL_BYTES_ONLY_NOT_PUBLICATION_OR_LIVE_FUNDING_AUTHORITY' (verifyDistributionCopies/receipt), 'READ_ONLY_SELF_CONSISTENT_NOT_STORE_MEMBERSHIP_PROOF' (closed proceeds basis), 'LOCAL_PREPARATION_ONLY_NOT_LIVE_FUNDING_AUTHORITY' (preparePayoutFunding, downstream). None of these objects, even fully valid and signed, authorize an actual on-chain fund movement -- there is a deliberate, repeated, hard stop between 'we prepared a signed payout authorization' and 'funds moved'. Whatever executes the real transfer/claim on Robinhood Chain is out of this unit's scope entirely (and, per the task's repo facts, is one of the deferred Phase-2 lines).

No live holder snapshot source. validateSnapshot only checks the SHAPE of a snapshot object (schema/authority/asset/chainId/tokenAddress/blockNumber/blockHash/finalized/directBalances) that is handed in by the caller; there is no code here that reads an RPC, an indexer, or any chain state to actually produce {recipient, directHkmnBalance} pairs for real HKMN holders. authority is literally 'INPUT_BOUND_CANDIDATE_NOT_AUTHENTICATED' -- the module explicitly does not authenticate that the snapshot reflects real chain state.

1024-recipient cap with no overflow/pagination path. WIDTH=1024 is a hard ceiling (assertCandidateArray throws above 1024, buildDistribution assumes exactly WIDTH leaves). If HKMN ever has more than 1024 non-zero holders, this entire pipeline cannot represent them in one distribution artifact, and there is no code here for splitting a cycle's proceeds across multiple 1024-leaf artifacts/payoutIds.

Two independent signing keys (owner approval, copy-verifier) are required per cycle, both via raw Ed25519 private-key signing (see manifest.test.mjs) -- there is no code here (or evidence of a service) that produces these signatures unattended. For a 20-minute autonomous loop this implies either a live signer service holding both private keys and rubber-stamping every cycle (defeating the 'owner approval' safeguard's purpose) or a human has to sign twice every cycle, which contradicts 'fully autonomous'.

No CLI/dashboard entry point. grep across the repo shows this unit is only referenced from (a) its own tests, (b) cycle-runner.mjs's two consumer methods, and (c) the Foundry FFI adapter script -- scripts/v4.mjs (the operator CLI mentioned in the repo facts) does not reference any distribution/* module. There is no 'distribute now' or 'show pending distribution' command an operator (or a future dashboard) could call.

No scheduling/interval/cron concept anywhere in this unit -- consistent with the repo facts that Phase 2 (automation, dashboard, adjustable interval) is deferred; this unit only ever processes ONE already-closed cycle at a time, on demand, driven entirely by function calls from a caller that must already know the cycleId/proceedsKey.

The 3-copy verification (primary/mirror/archive) checks byte-equality of copies handed to it in-process; it does not itself fetch copies from 3 physically-separate storage locations, so it provides no protection against a single process that fabricates all 3 'independent' copies from the same in-memory artifact (as every test and the adapter script does) -- true independence would require this to be called from 3 separate storage reads, which is not demonstrated or enforced anywhere in this unit.

suspicions.note: OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY is a literal hardcoded Ed25519 DER hex string in source, with no test-vs-production key separation visible in this file (no env var, no config lookup). If this same constant is reused for a real owner key in a live deployment, rotating or environment-scoping it would require a code change, not a config change. Should be confirmed against how production wiring (outside this unit) supplies keys.

Same hardcoding pattern for DISTRIBUTION_VERIFIER_PUBLIC_KEY -- worth checking whether this key pair is meant to be Anthropic/Hookemon-operated infra distinct from the owner, or is actually the same person/process wearing two hats (which would make the 'independent verifier' signature largely ceremonial).

Hardcoded 'requirementsRevision !== 56' check. This silently and permanently locks this module to Phase-1 ledgers. If Phase 2 (revision 57 per repo facts) ships and reuses this reconcile.mjs file unmodified, every real cycle will fail with 'closed proceeds basis requirements revision is invalid' -- worth flagging to whoever migrates Phase 2 onto this code.

Reaches three directories up and across a package boundary ('../../../contracts/tooling/payout/canonical-merkle-sum.mjs') from packages/runner into packages/contracts/tooling with a bare relative path and no package.json dependency/workspace reference visible in this file. Fragile to future repo reorganization; also means packages/runner cannot be published/vendored independently of packages/contracts without breaking this import.

DEPTH=10 / WIDTH=1024 is a compile-time constant baked into both the JS tree builder and (presumably) the Solidity verifier it must match; this file does not itself assert or document where the matching Solidity-side constant lives, so a future change to one side without the other would silently desynchronize proof depth (verifyProof would just produce wrong roots, not throw, unless siblingHashes.length happens to still be checked, which it is at line 253 -- but a Solidity-side DEPTH change would not be caught by this JS file at all).

The check `built.root.sum !== candidate.totalAmountAtomicUSDG` happens AFTER buildDistribution() has already run (i.e. after all 1024 leaf/node keccaks). Since totalAmountAtomicUSDG was already cross-checked against entries in reconcile.mjs and entries feed 1:1 into the tree, this late check is effectively unreachable defense-in-depth rather than a real failure mode -- confirm this is intentional belt-and-suspenders and not evidence that the two totals can actually diverge via some path not covered by tests.

signedApproval()/signedVerificationReceipt() sign with raw private keys held directly in the test file. This is fine for a test fixture, but it is the ONLY place in the reviewed code that shows how an approval/verification signature gets produced end to end -- there is no production 'signer' module in this unit, reinforcing the autonomyGaps entry about unattended signing.

Only ONE recipient (RECIPIENT, index 0) is exercised in the Foundry-integration path, with a hardcoded amountAtomicUSDG of '10' equal to the entire fixture return. The Solidity/JS Merkle-sum parity is therefore proven for a single non-empty leaf plus 1023 empty leaves, not for a realistic multi-holder, multi-index (e.g. sparse index 511/1023-style) tree -- the sparse-index cases are only exercised on the JS side (holder-candidate.test.mjs) and never cross-checked against Solidity in this repo as far as this unit shows.

merkleTree.hashFunction: keccak256 (from-scratch Keccak-f[1600] BigInt implementation in canonical-merkle-sum.mjs, not node:crypto)

keyFacts.manifestHeadLayoutBytes: 320-byte head (10 words incl. length prefix at offset 256/288) then 128 bytes per entry (index uint16, recipient address, amount uint256, directBalance uint256)
keyFacts.custodyInvariant: returnAccount === cycleVaultAccount; {operationsTrigger, cycleVaultAccount, policyAccount} pairwise distinct

keyFacts.adapterStandaloneRun: Confirmed: `node test/integration/phase-one-local-loop-adapter.mjs <40-hex hook> <chainId>` from packages/runner runs to completion and prints ABI-encoded hex; exercised with a synthetic 0xaa...aa hook and chainId 4663.

openQuestions: Where (in an unreviewed part of the repo, or nowhere yet) is the pro-rata amount for each holder actually computed from a live total supply / live proceeds figure, including the rounding/remainder rule? This unit only verifies a pre-computed allocation, it does not compute one.

Who/what is meant to hold and use the two Ed25519 private keys (owner approval, distribution verifier) in an unattended 20-minute-cycle deployment, given every schema explicitly marks its output as non-live/non-funding? Is a human expected to sign every cycle, defeating 'fully autonomous', or is there a planned automated signer (and if so, does that collapse the owner-approval safeguard to a rubber stamp)?

Is the hardcoded OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY / DISTRIBUTION_VERIFIER_PUBLIC_KEY in manifest.mjs a real production key or a fixture/test key? The variable names and the surrounding 'FIXTURE_OWNER_SIGNATURE' / schema names ('hookemon.fixture-distribution-approval.v1') strongly suggest fixture-only, but this should be confirmed before any live use.
What happens once real HKMN holder counts exceed 1024? Is multi-artifact/multi-payoutId chunking planned, and if so where -- this unit has no support for it at all.

Where does '3 independent copies' actually get its independence from in a real deployment (separate machines/buckets/signers), since this unit only checks byte-equality of whatever 3 objects it is handed and cannot itself detect that all 3 came from the same single source?

Given requirementsRevision is hardcoded to 56, what is the migration plan for this exact file when Phase 2 (revision 57, per repo facts) becomes the live policy -- is reconcile.mjs expected to be forked, parameterized, or replaced outright?
